metadata.reason: Primary title/name of the artifact

metadata.value: an opensource hardware and software weed detector that uses entirely off-the-shelf componentry, very simple green-detection algorithms (with capacity to upgrade to in-crop detection) and 3D printable parts. OWL integrates weed detection on a Raspberry Pi with a relay control board or custom driver board, in a custom designed case so you can attach any 12V solenoid, relay, lightbulb or device for low-cost, simple and open-source site-specific weed control.

metadata.evidence:
Welcome to the OpenWeedLocator (OWL) project, an opensource hardware and software weed detector that uses
entirely off-the-shelf componentry, very simple green-detection algorithms (with capacity to upgrade to
in-crop detection) and 3D printable parts. OWL integrates weed detection on a Raspberry Pi with a relay
control board or custom driver board, in a custom designed case so you can attach any 12V solenoid, relay, lightbulb or 
device for low-cost, simple and open-source site-specific weed control.
metadata.reason: Describes the purpose and functionality of the artifact

metadata.evidence:
#### Investigating image-based fallow weed detection performance on Raphanus sativus and Avena sativa at speeds up to 30 km/h

The performance of the OWL from 5 - 30 km/h with different cameras and on broadleaf and grass 'weeds' was tested and
published
in [Computers and Electronics in Agriculture](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0168169923008074).
metadata.reason: Second scientific publication with performance benchmarks for the OWL

metadata.value: The current Raspberry Pi HQ Camera + latest software combination provided a recall of 74.8% at 5 km/h and 50.5 % at 30 km/h. Recall of up to 95.7% at 5 km/h was achieved by the global shutter Arducam AR0234.

current Raspberry Pi HQ Camera + latest software combination provided a recall of 74.8% at 5 km/h and 50.5 % at 30 km/h.

metadata.value: site-specific weed detection and control (green detection, green-on-brown and green-on-green)
metadata.evidence: So how does OWL actually detect the weeds and trigger the relay control board? It all starts by taking in the colour image from the camera using OpenCV and splitting it into its component channels: Red (R), Green (G) and Blue (B) (RGB) or loading and converting into the hue, saturation and value (HSV) colourspace.
metadata.reason: Describes the core task the artifact performs (image-based weed detection)

metadata.value: Excess Green (ExG), HSV thresholding, combined ExG+HSV (ExHSV) algorithms
metadata.evidence:
A range of green detection
algorithms were tested including ExG (excess green 2g - r - b, developed by Woebbecke et al. 1995), a hue, saturation
and value (HSV) threshold and a combined ExG + HSV algorithm.
metadata.reason: Names the specific detection algorithms used/evaluated by the artifact
